consistency_check.note: Programmatically verified by this generator (not a manual eyeball check) before writing status=COMPLETE. Every one of the 61 runs below -- selftest, all 18 1 GiB correctness/perf/storage combinations, all 9 1 GiB scale-sensitive crash scenarios, all 31 128 MiB adversarial/logic crash scenarios, and both backup-footprint runs -- shares this exact source_commit and extension_binary_sha256. This corrects the prior PARTIAL round, which mixed results from three different executable commits (833ed33, b03243f, a117ce2) into one invalid COMPLETE claim.

scope_note: PoC-level unbiased comparison of three storage backends for a DROP-recovery snapshot artifact, sharing the exact same Protocol B boundary/marker choreography and WAL-replay correctness oracle Step 7 already qualified. Not production-wired: no production SnapshotStore backend, no storage_backend CHECK constraint change, no public API/GUC change.
corrections_since_prior_partial_round: commits_replayed==copy_window_commits: eliminated the underlying SIGTERM race with a durable ledger table (poc_bench_writer_ledger) instead of relaxing the invariant to >=. Strict equality now verified on every one of the 18 matrix rows (see commits_strict_equal in each row below).

heap_v1 restore_ms was a no-op measurement (restored_tbl aliased to the artifact table). Added restore_heap_v1: a real, timed CREATE TABLE ... AS SELECT FROM the artifact, materializing a genuinely separate table -- restore_ms and wal_bytes_restore for heap_v1 are now real, nonzero, measured costs.

WAL amplification was inferred from timing/architecture. Added direct pg_current_wal_insert_lsn()/pg_wal_lsn_diff() measurement per phase (materialize/persist/restore) for every run -- see wal_bytes_* fields below.

Backup-footprint was inferred. Added a real pg_basebackup-based measurement mode: one cluster/source table, baseline backup, then each backend's real incremental byte delta, artifact reset between backends so deltas are independent -- see backup_footprint below.

Manifest fields were recorded but mostly unvalidated at restore. Added validate_manifest_binding: format_version, backend, pg_major, arch, system_identifier, current db oid, encoding, tracking_id, semantic_fingerprint_format_version, schema fingerprint (column order/type/typmod/collation via pg_attribute, not a bare information_schema string), row_count, and a cross-check of boundary_lsn/boundary_xid against the durable WAL-decode ledger (commit_log) -- all fail-closed on mismatch.
verify_restore now also checks table owner and ACL, not just row count/fingerprint/schema/TOAST-hash.

in_db_logged_zstd's adversarial matrix was missing missing_chunk/manifest_mismatch runs (the tamper logic already supported it, it was simply never executed) -- now run and passing. Added two new crash points applicable to both zstd backends: row_count_mismatch (isolates the row_count cross-check specifically) and chunk_order_mismatch (proves scrambled chunk ordering is caught).

Three further real bugs found and fixed during this correction round itself: persist_in_db_logged_zstd/persist_external_zstd computed manifest row_count/logical_bytes from the LIVE mutating source table instead of the snapshot-consistent ground truth (caught by the new row_count validation); backup-footprint's DELETE-based cleanup between backend measurements did not reclaim poc_bench_chunks' physical space, contaminating the next backend's delta (fixed with DROP+recreate); the writer loop's per-statement bare commands died on the very first transient failure (a genuine, expected id collision across a crash+retry boundary) because the ledger rewrite lost the errexit-tolerance the old && chaining provided as a side effect -- fixed with explicit || true, restoring tolerance without reintroducing the original race.

matrix_1gib.description: 3 backends x 3 data shapes x 2 reps, all real 1 GiB scale, all on the single verified-consistent source_commit/extension_binary_sha256 above. commits_strict_equal is true for all 18 rows (copy_window_commits == commits_replayed exactly, not >=).

crash_matrix_1gib_scale_sensitive.description: Crash points re-run at real 1 GiB scale because they are scale-sensitive (a real materializing statement must be caught genuinely active; multi-chunk behavior only appears at this scale). All re-run on the consistent commit after the writer-subshell fix -- the original run of this exact matrix on this same commit is what surfaced that bug (100% failure, 5/5, before the fix).

crash_matrix_logic_128mib.description: Adversarial/logic crash points where scale does not change what is being proven. Now includes full parity for in_db_logged_zstd (missing_chunk, manifest_mismatch previously untested) plus two new crash points (row_count_mismatch, chunk_order_mismatch) for both zstd backends. All 31 PASS on the consistent commit.
crash_matrix_logic_128mib.known_gap_disclosed: temp_chunk_write_crash/chunk_fsync_done/manifest_fsync_before/after/parent_dir_fsync_after are modeled as an abrupt kill of the writing step (or a real pg_ctl -m immediate crash+restart for DB-side points). This proves incomplete userspace state is never mistaken for valid. It does not prove real fsync-durability against an actual host power loss, which this environment cannot safely test.

backup_footprint.description: Real pg_basebackup byte deltas (-Fp -X none, data directory contents only), not inferred. Baseline = source table alone; each backend's delta measured independently (artifact reset between measurements via DROP+recreate, not DELETE, so physical space is genuinely reclaimed).

capacity_preflight_10gib.filesystem: /dev/vda3 (single filesystem; PG data dir and external artifact dir share it in this environment)
capacity_preflight_10gib.method: Linear projection from measured 1 GiB end-of-run ephemeral_disk_bytes (DATA dir, du -sb) + external_artifact_bytes_at_cleanup, x10, plus an estimated transient WORK_ROOT overhead (raw COPY BINARY stream + chunk staging + restore reconstruction) not captured by ephemeral_disk_bytes since it is measured on $DATA only.
capacity_preflight_10gib.reasoning: Available (43 GB) is less than half of even the low-estimate worst-case single-run peak (75 GB), let alone with the +8 GB safety reserve or the additional transient WORK_ROOT overhead. Did not attempt any 10 GiB run. Did not delete unrelated files/other targets to force capacity.
runnable_when_capacity_available: (repeat each with rep2 for the required second trial; run sequentially, not in parallel, so the harness's own cleanup() reclaims disk between runs)
capacity_preflight_10gib.carried_over_note: Capacity projection not recomputed after the correction round below; the correctness/measurement fixes in that round do not change how much physical disk PostgreSQL actually uses for these operations, so the original projection (from the PARTIAL round measurements) remains a valid basis for the BLOCKED_BY_CAPACITY determination. Still not run: no 10 GiB round was attempted.

prior_partial_round.partial_notice: This round mixed PASS results from different executable harness commits into one matrix (9 runs on 833ed33, 3 on b03243f, 6 heap_v1 reruns on a117ce2; crash matrix on b03243f) -- not a valid basis for a COMPLETE determination regardless of whether intervening fixes were correctness-relevant. Additionally: commits_replayed>=copy_window_commits relaxed a real SIGTERM race instead of eliminating it; heap_v1 restore_ms was a no-op measurement, not real; WAL amplification and backup-footprint were inferred, not measured; manifest binding fields were recorded but mostly unvalidated at restore; in_db_logged_zstd was missing missing_chunk/manifest_mismatch adversarial runs. This record is kept as an accurate historical account of what actually ran, not deleted or rewritten. A new evidence record on one consistent commit supersedes it.

harness_corrections_during_this_round.change: compression_ratio metric always recorded 0 (bc not installed in this environment); switched to awk.

Two real bugs from the first crash-mode smoke runs: establish_boundary_and_materialize's oracle-shadow bookkeeping had no ON CONFLICT/DROP-IF-EXISTS guard (crash-mode retries call it twice against the same source table); and restore_in_db_logged_zstd/restore_external_zstd die() internally via a direct exit call, which a bare '|| flag=1' at the call site cannot catch -- fixed with subshell+if wrapping.
load_ground_truth_from_rawfile had the same not-safely-re-callable bug as the oracle shadow fix above.

persist_in_db_logged_zstd/persist_external_zstd had no error checking on their manifest-row INSERT, so duplicate_retry's expected PK-collision failure was silently swallowed under errexit suspension rather than propagated; added explicit die() guards.

commits_replayed==copy_window_commits was too strict: a real 1 GiB run hit commits_replayed=64 vs copy_window_commits=61, root-caused to the writer loop's counter file being written AFTER a statement already committed durably to WAL, racing against SIGTERM during shutdown. Data was never lost; only the writer's own self-reported count could lag. Relaxed to >=.

cleanup() never purged the bulky rawstream_*.bin/chunks_*//restore_*/ working files (not evidence), which accumulated to 37G across one session's runs and caused three otherwise-correct 1 GiB reruns to fail on real ENOSPC. Extended cleanup() to remove them under the same POC_KEEP gate as DATA/PGLIB.

heap_v1's artifact_bytes was always recorded 0 (no separate persist phase populates it), biasing the storage comparison. Added a direct pg_total_relation_size measurement for heap_v1's own artifact table.

matrix_1gib.description: 3 backends x 3 data shapes x 2 reps, all real 1 GiB scale, all PASS against the harness state noted per row (source_commit field). Ordinary/toast bad-compressing shapes reuse Step 7's proven generators (narrow per-row-salted hash chain; 512-md5-chain incompressible bytea); good_compress is new for Step 8 (highly redundant repeat()'d text).

crash_matrix_1gib_scale_sensitive.description: Crash points re-run at real 1 GiB scale specifically because they are scale-sensitive (a real materializing statement must be caught genuinely active, and multi-chunk behavior only appears at this scale with 15-17 chunks vs 1-2 at 128 MiB).

crash_matrix_logic_128_256mib.description: Adversarial/logic crash points where scale does not change what is being proven (tamper detection, fsync/rename ordering, split-state, orphan-GC). Run at 128-256 MiB for speed; final (latest, post-fix) outcome shown per unique backend/crash_point pair -- earlier FAILs during development that led to the harness_corrections_during_this_round entries above are not hidden, only the corrected re-run result is reported as authoritative here.
crash_matrix_logic_128_256mib.honesty_note_on_fsync_points: temp_chunk_write_crash/chunk_fsync_done/manifest_fsync_before/after/parent_dir_fsync_after are modeled as an abrupt process kill of the writing step (for DB-side points, a real pg_ctl -m immediate crash+restart). This proves incomplete userspace state (a partial temp file, a not-yet-renamed chunk) is never mistaken for valid. It does NOT prove real fsync-durability against an actual host power loss, since this environment cannot safely power-cycle itself and a normal process kill does not revert a rename() the kernel has already accepted into its page cache.

prior_partial_round.note: Preserved as an accurate historical record of what actually ran during the PARTIAL round (mixed commits 833ed33/b03243f/a117ce2). Superseded by the top-level COMPLETE evidence above, which re-ran everything on one consistent commit after all corrections.
